text: this: [Image #1] [Image #2] what is the difference of these two images
resolution: The two screenshots showed the grid problem: zoomed IN the iso grid is a bold clean lattice that fills the view; zoomed OUT it's a tiny speck near centre and the map reads grid-less. Cause: IsoGrid drew a FIXED 26-tile (~52m) patch around the camera with 0.08m-thick lines, so when zoomed out over the large map the patch covered a sliver and the thin lines fell below a pixel. Replaced it with an adaptive-LOD grid: the cell size, the coverage extent, and the line thickness all scale with the eye distance (stage.distance()) — 1-tile cells up close, coarse 8/16/32-tile cells far out — with the line count bounded (~114 boxes), the centre snapped to the cell step so lines stay world-anchored and don't shimmer on pan, and steps kept to nice 1·2·4·8 multiples of the 1 tile = 1 m grid so they always fall on real cells. Committed 696381509, bundles clean.
